column1: India sells medicines to around two hundred countries.
That's why you hear it called the pharmacy of the world.
But open one antibiotic capsule and look at the white powder inside.
That's the actual medicine... and there's a fair chance its journey began in China.
The rest of the capsule is just there to carry it to you.
Now think back to the Corona days.
You remember them.
Not the lockdown yet — this is three weeks before it.
The third of March, twenty twenty.
In China, the city of Wuhan has been locked down for almost six weeks.
Here in India, there are only a handful of cases so far.
Delhi.
A two-page government order goes out, and if you run a medicine company, your phone starts ringing.
Thirteen medicine ingredients, and the medicines made from them, can't leave India without a licence.
Paracetamol is one of them.
Wait.
India?
The pharmacy of the world... locking its own doors?
Yes.
And the reason was Corona.
Wuhan sits in a Chinese province called Hubei... and the whole province was shut down.
Reports at the time said many of the ingredients on that list came from that one place.
So here's the question I want to answer for you today.
If India makes medicine for the world... who makes the powder inside India's medicine?
And before you worry — this isn't about the quality of your medicines.
It's about who controls the supply.
